analysis.title: Monday set up for the Binky bounce: from sell the rip to buy the dip in just 15 trading days
key_insights: Deutsche Bank's Binky Chadha downgraded Tech to neutral about three weeks ago, ahead of a sharp rotation out of the sector. Fifteen trading days later he is moving back to overweight.
Mega-cap growth and Tech have underperformed the rest of the S&P 500 by more than 16 percentage points in three weeks, taking relative performance to the bottom of its decade-long trend channel.
Deutsche Bank notes Tech has staged five V-shaped recoveries from similar relative levels in the past 2.5 years. The last five rotations into Tech saw the sector gain an average of 38%.
This rotation is somewhat shallower than the previous five, but Chadha judges it fits the pattern.
Tech positioning has fallen from elevated levels to the 40th percentile, so the sector has moved from crowded to unloved.
Current positioning implies Tech earnings growth of roughly 10%, versus 47% in Q3 and consensus expectations of 36% by the end of next year.
Tech leads in Q3 revenue growth, and top-line growth estimates have been revised up over the past month (FactSet).

The median S&P 500 company is growing earnings by 14.4%, near two-decade highs outside recession rebounds. Excluding Tech and Energy, earnings growth is still 12%, which argues against the view that the earnings boom is only AI-driven.

The note says investors are positioned for a dramatic earnings slowdown that has not yet appeared in the numbers, with the word 'Yet' implying it could.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech has moved from crowded to unloved (40th percentile positioning) while Q3 earnings growth of 47% and upward revisions to revenue estimates remain intact. Five prior V-shaped recoveries from similar levels averaged a 38% gain.
tension_points.bear_case: Positioning implies investors expect a sharp earnings slowdown to about 10% growth. The current rotation is somewhat shallower than prior ones, so the historical pattern may not repeat.
